Risk Description:
NIC Group defines
Compliance or Regulatory
Risk as the potential of loss
arising from non-compliance
with laws, rules, regulations,
obligatory practices /
standards, contractual
agreements, or other legal
requirements including the
effectiveness of preventing
and handling litigation. It is
not actively or deliberately
pursued in the expectation of
a profit or return, but occurs
in the normal course of our
business operations.
The Group meets high
standards of compliance
with legal, regulatory and
policy requirements in
all business dealings and
transactions as required
by our five main regulators
(CBK, BoT, BoU, CMA
and IRA), amongst other
regulators, and Government
Agencies.
Assessment:
The Compliance
Department identifies and
monitors the key risks
and is responsible for
ensuring that the day to day
business controls comply
with applicable legislation
plus regulations and are
in line with best practices.
On a quarterly basis a
compliance obligations
register per key functions
is updated to confirm
adherence.
Internal and external legal
counsel work closely with
business units to identify
areas of existing and
potential regulatory/legal
risks and actively manage
them to reduce the Group’s
exposures.
Business unit heads have
the responsibility and
accountability of managing
legal and regulatory risks
relating to their units on
a day to day basis with
assistance / advice and
oversight from the Legal
and Compliance functions.
Senior management and
Board Risk Management
Committee receive
the Risk Management
Department’s opinions /
reports on the strength of
the Group’s Compliance
Risk Framework to enable
them to determine whether
it’s under control and where
not, tracks significant
corrective actions closures.
Mitigation:
The Board of Directors and Senior
Management through the Group’s Code of
Conduct & Ethics sets the “tone at the top” for
a culture of integrity beginning with concern
for what is right (including compliance
to policy and the law) in all our business
considerations, decisions and actions.
All employees attest to this Code, which
include our values, when they join the Group,
and thereafter periodically, indicating that
they have understood it, and that they have
complied with its provisions.
Other Compliance mitigants:
• Periodic tracking of compliance to
general banking laws, regulations and
reporting requirements.
• Approved compliance policy and
program in place to provide guidance on
compliance risk management.
• Robust policies, programs and systems
designed to manage the Know Your
Customer (KYC) and Anti-Money
Laundering (AML) risks as envisaged
in the Proceeds of Crime & Anti-Money
Laundering Act, and related Regulations.
• Upgraded account opening requirements
and customer transaction screening
procedures to meet the stringent
requirements stipulated therein related
laws and regulations.
• Reporting of suspicious and other
transactions such as cash transactions
over regulatory thresholds, is done as
required by the law and policy standards.
• Periodic due diligence on correspondent
banking counterparties, and meet KYC /
AML obligations to them continuously.
• Staff are trained when they join the Group
and periodically certified as such in line
with the law.
• Code of Conduct & Ethics covering good
Values, and Conduct issues such sAnti-
Bribery, customer confidentiality matters,
etc.
